body.name: finite monotone primal-dual certificate algorithm
body.construction:
Given \(\mathfrak E\) and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate deterministically all finite binary-rational candidates consisting of lower and upper terminal-envelope widths \(\delta\), small-information cutoffs \(\eta\), an inner score box and a strictly larger guard box, time and allocation-clock meshes, a finite rational control net in the allocation simplex, a finite rational prior net in \(\Delta_M\) containing every point mass, a rational near-Bayes retention tolerance, a partition of a truncated standardized Gaussian box into rational cells, and an outward-rounding precision.  Put \(c_H=H+H^2/2\).  For the normalized posterior terminal payoff use
\[
\Omega_\delta(d)=\min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+2Kc_H\right)d\right\}.
\]
For each prior \(\lambda\), let \(C_G\) be the computable maximum of \(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\) on the guard box, write \(S=(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m)/C_G\), and scale the lower and upper regularized versions of \(F_\lambda\) by \(C_G^{-1}\).  For the resulting scaled unnormalized datum \(Sg\), use throughout
\[
\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)=
\min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+3Kc_H\right)d\right\}.
\]
Propagate the scaled values backward on the viable state cells and undo the scale at the initial state.  At a state cell of diameter \(d\), the interval interpolant is the barycentric sum of the vertex intervals enlarged by \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)\).  Use this same scaled-datum modulus in state and control-net estimates whenever terminal continuity is invoked, in mollification error, in Bellman residual and finite-horizon accumulation, in every fixed-policy and point-mass-oracle recursion, and in the corresponding entries of the actual certificate ledger; when its linear expression is at least one, use the range bound one.

For every control-net point, scenario, and retained Gaussian cell, outward-round the cell probability, enclose the entire image of that cell under the score-clock transition, multiply the probability interval by the resulting continuation interval, and sum outward.  Use the interval \([0,1]\) only for transitions outside the guard box and for omitted Gaussian-tail mass.  A rational compactly supported mollification of the multilinear interpolants is checked cell by cell against the reference-law Bellman operators; Taylor's formula with integral remainder supplies a certified time-discretization and control residual, and the same recursion supplies its finite-horizon accumulated bound.  Run the identical validated recursion at every point-mass prior to enclose the regularized versions of \(c_m\).  Retain every enumerated grid policy certified to be near-Bayes at some prior-net point, solve outward-rounded rational primal and dual scenario-risk linear programs over those columns, and independently re-evaluate the selected finite policy mixture by a fixed-policy interval recursion.  Extend the dual search from the prior net using the \(\ell_1\)-Lipschitz bound for the Bayes-regret functional.

Form a ledger from the actual certified terminal-regularization, guard-exit, time-discretization, scaled-datum interpolation and control-mesh, Gaussian-cell, Gaussian-tail, mollification and Bellman-residual accumulation, oracle and linear-program, recovered-policy, prior-net, and rounding contributions, with every scaled-datum continuity contribution recomputed from \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta\).  Replace each lower endpoint by the maximum and each upper endpoint by the minimum over all candidates examined so far.  Accept the first candidate for which the sum of the applicable certified ledger bounds is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\); call the resulting cumulative endpoints \(\underline V_{\varepsilon}\) and \(\overline V_{\varepsilon}\).
